newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable despite double stem blockage.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable despite double stem blockage.

text.p: Naphtha prices were barely changed in afternoon Tokyo trade on Thursday despite news that Algeria would not give permission to load double stem naphtha cargoes out of Skikda for the time being, traders said.

But moving single stem, or 25,000-tonne, cargoes to Asia is not as economical as moving double stem or 50,000-tonne, cargoes, cargoes originally earmarked for Asia may stay in Europe, traders said. Some dealers, as a result, may need to cover their short positions in Asia, but the decision by state-owned Sonatrach has yet to have any real impact on the market, they said.
Asian naphtha started to lose ground in late March amid an influx of arbitrage cargoes from the West as well as weaker crude oil prices.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half July was quoted at $208.50/209.50 per tonne after a first-half July contract was sold to a U.S. oil trader at $209.00 on Wednesday.

In middle distillates, a Japanese refiner bought about 25,000 tonnes of spot jet cargo at about $1.30 over the mean of Singapore quotes per barrel. The cargo will be delivered to Osaka, western Japan, in early June to be supplied to the Kansai International Airport, a trader with the refiner said.
